ai.description: The saltwater crocodile reaches 6–7 meters. It is olive-green or grey with a broad snout, lacking the enlarged fourth-tooth notch of other species. It possesses fewer nuchal scales than other crocs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable way to distinguish the Saltwater Crocodile is by its broad snout, which lacks the prominent bony ridges found in front of the eyes on the Mugger crocodile.
ai.habitat: *Crocodylus porosus* inhabits coastal mangrove forests, tidal estuaries, and river deltas across the Indian subcontinent, restricted to low-lying, near-sea-level elevations.
ai.behavior: Saltwater crocodiles are primarily nocturnal hunters that use stealth and powerful lunges to ambush prey from the water's edge.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Crocodylus porosus* is oviparous, nesting during the monsoon (May–August). Females build mound nests and lay a clutch of 40–60 eggs in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: In the Indian subcontinent, *Crocodylus porosus* inhabits the coastal mangroves and estuaries of Odisha, West Bengal, and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands at sea level.
